description: WO-E5: the Blender region in the dashboard, rendered from GET /api/v2/capabilities and filled by the preload bridge. The real Electron window announces what is on this box (x-scruple-host-apps), the server draws a Blender region because it was told there is a Blender, and everything inside the region is a reading taken on this machine: the version out of the running binary, the addon's enabled state out of the Blender that loaded it, and a bridge's ComfyUI address out of that bridge's own preferences, compared against the port the gate actually allocated.

steps.note: required:false so a bridge that cannot answer does not stop the run before the DOM is read. That is the whole point of the fake-bridge mutation: the REGION still draws, because its applicability comes from a header the main process sets on the session and a lying preload cannot touch it — and every READING inside it goes red, because a renderer-local stub cannot start a Blender.

assert.note: the readings came from the main process — a renderer-local stub cannot know this pid or this nonce, and cannot start a Blender
⚑ THE WORK ORDER'S GATE. The server sent this region because the window announced a Blender on this box; it is absent by default and there is no branch that draws it any other way.
`measured` is set only when the bridge answered. With no bridge it is `unavailable` and with an error it is `refused`; there is no fourth state and no default.

⚑ THE SPLIT THAT MAKES THIS HONEST. The SERVER said a Blender region applies; the version inside it was read by the DRIVER from `blender --version` before the app started, and independently by the app from the same binary. No server could know it and no static mock could invent it.
the app's reading against the driver's, both taken from the binary itself rather than from a manifest, a bl_info or a path
read out of a running Blender's own preferences, not off the disk we installed to
WO-E3's discriminator: only the blender_manifest.toml path produces a `bl_ext.<repo>.<id>` module name, so this names the file Blender actually read

⚑ A COMPARISON BETWEEN TWO THINGS NOBODY HERE INVENTED: an address read out of a bridge addon's own preferences inside a running Blender, and the port the gate allocated from the kernel. The gate binds port 0, so this string exists nowhere until it is allocated.
not merely 'a bridge was found' — the address on the leaf of this reading is the URL the launch step reported
docs/STATE.md §0: a dashboard that quietly omitted an app would be the failure mode. The REGION is what appears and disappears with the machine; the APP is listed either way, with the reason.
the new region's heading is the canon's ALL-CAPS section header, measured by the layout engine after the cascade — nothing here restyles anything, and no pixel was read
the route refuses rather than guessing when capabilities cannot be reached; a green run must not be a refusal that happened to contain the right strings
WO-D5's control, unchanged by this work order: adding a region must not have made the dashboard draw everything

auditNote:
The mutations split into two groups, and the split is the design.

THE ANNOUNCEMENT. `announce-without-blender` and `announce-nothing` leave a real 4.2.23 sitting in this repo's tree and change only what the window SAYS. Both make the region vanish, which is what proves the shape follows the announcement — a build that drew a Blender region because the profile was `desktop` would survive both. They are not redundant: one says "I looked and there is none", the other says nothing at all, and the capabilities answer's `reason` differs because the fixes differ.

THE MACHINE. `blender-vanishes` points every place the app looks at an empty directory. The announcement is then honest — there is no Blender — and the region goes with it. This is the work order's own control and it is not a flag: `resolveBinary()` finds nothing because there is nothing.

THE READINGS. `no-addon-profile` keeps the same binary and the same version and takes the addon away, so only the addon assertions may move. `bridge-elsewhere` keeps the bridge installed and configured and simply never points it at the gate, so only the bridge assertions may move — and the state must become `elsewhere`, never `none`, because a bridge that exists and points somewhere else is a different fact with a different fix.

`fake-bridge` is the measure of what the DOM is worth alone. The region still DRAWS — its applicability comes from a header the main process sets on the session, which a lying preload cannot touch — and every reading inside it goes red, because a renderer-local stub cannot start a Blender.
